body:
The current test setup is really not ideal in my view. 

1. Right now there are a lot of documentation specific tests -- who needs that ?
2. There are a bunch of other potential test issues ? Can you investigate?

@sepo-agent /answer

comments.body:
I investigated the current setup. There is no broader parent/tracking issue referenced in #409, and the suite is currently green: `cd .agent && npm test` passes `714/714` in ~14s.

The core problem is real, but I’d frame it as **test taxonomy and coupling**, not simply “too many docs tests”.

Current shape:
- `.agent/package.json` has one catch-all test command that builds and runs every compiled test file: [`npm test`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/package.json#L6-L10).
- CI builds once, then `npm test` builds again, so CI does redundant work: [`test-scripts.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/test-scripts.yml#L17-L28).
- CI also has separate Ruby validation steps for YAML and `GH_TOKEN` policy, outside the TypeScript test harness: [`test-scripts.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/test-scripts.yml#L30-L64).
- There are 74 test files under one flat `.agent/src/__tests__` directory.
- The docs-specific validation file is small, but very policy-specific: frontmatter, no README, no leading H1, relative links: [`docs-validation.test.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/__tests__/docs-validation.test.ts#L47-L101).
- The bigger docs issue is hidden inside `envelope.test.ts`: it mixes prompt checks, workflow/action fixture checks, doc content assertions, and actual envelope model tests in one 2,284-line file. Example docs assertions are at [`L235-L241`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/__tests__/envelope.test.ts#L235-L241), [`L488-L498`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/__tests__/envelope.test.ts#L488-L498), [`L1434-L1465`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/__tests__/envelope.test.ts#L1434-L1465), and [`L1744-L1765`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/__tests__/envelope.test.ts#L1744-L1765).
- There is a lot of integration-style harness repetition: 30 test files spawn subprocesses, 40 create temp dirs, and 33 touch `process.env`. Example: [`extract-context-cli.test.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/__tests__/extract-context-cli.test.ts#L29-L63).

Recommended redesign:

1. Keep docs tests, but demote them to a small `check:docs` lane.
   - Keep link/frontmatter/nav-shape checks.
   - Remove brittle “docs must mention phrase X” assertions from runtime/workflow tests unless they protect a real public contract.
   - Move remaining docs checks out of the main runtime test suite.

2. Split the suite into lanes:
   - `test:unit`: pure TypeScript logic, no subprocesses, no git, no repo fixture files.
   - `test:cli`: CLI subprocess tests using built `dist`.
   - `test:workflow`: workflow/action/prompt contract checks.
   - `check:docs`: docs structure/link checks only.
   - `check:shell`: shell syntax and shell behavior checks.
   - `test:ci`: one composed command for CI.

3. Break up `envelope.test.ts`.
   - Put envelope schema/model tests near `envelope`.
   - Put workflow/action contract tests in a workflow fixture test file.
   - Put prompt contract tests in a prompt fixture test file.
   - Move doc assertions into docs checks or delete them.

4. Replace ad hoc harness code with shared helpers.
   - `withTempDir`
   - `runCli`
   - `fakeGh`
   - `withEnv`
   - Git fixture helpers for bare repo/worktree tests

5. Move CI’s Ruby checks into typed Node checks.
   - The repo already depends on `yaml`.
   - Keeping workflow validation in TypeScript makes it easier to run locally and keeps policy checks in the same ecosystem.

6. Fix CI redundancy.
   - CI should run `npm ci`, `npm run build`, then lane commands that do not rebuild unless explicitly needed.

I would not delete all docs tests. I would delete or move **content-coupled documentation assertions** and keep only cheap structural checks that prevent broken docs navigation/links. The larger win is making test failures answer “what broke?” immediately: unit behavior, CLI behavior, workflow contract, shell syntax, or docs hygiene.

---
